ai.description: This large constrictor reaches 5m. It features dark, rectangular, reddish-brown blotches on a tan background and two distinct dark lines extending from the snout through each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish the Burmese Python (*Python bivittatus*) by its dark, arrowhead-shaped head marking that extends forward to the snout, unlike the *Python molurus* (Indian Python).
ai.habitat: Burmese pythons inhabit tropical rainforests, marshes, and river valleys across the Indian subcontinent, typically remaining below 1,500 meters in dense, humid cover.
ai.behavior: Burmese pythons are primarily nocturnal ambush predators that remain motionless for long periods, waiting to strike at passing prey before constricting it.
ai.reproductionNotes: Burmese pythons are oviparous, laying 12–50 eggs in a single annual clutch. Breeding typically occurs during the cooler months, from December to April.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Burmese python inhabits the moist forests and wetlands of Northeast India, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to sea level across the Indo-Burmese biogeographic zone.
